_note: Declarative regression cases for the health engine (shared/health/health.py). Each maps to a MAINTAINER regression case; no real data — the engine reads repo structure + the placeholder ledger.

evals.name: clean_repo_has_no_blocking_issues
evals._note: Was `readiness_band: strong`, which was FALSE when this eval was first executed (2026-08-17): the scan reported `not_ready`. The cause turned out NOT to be a saturated metric, as I first assumed, but 44 warnings of which 43 were health.py's own false negative — it read routing.skills and never routing.atom_routes, so every correctly-registered atom was flagged 'not referenced'. With that fixed and teacher-core given the evals/ dir it lacked, the band IS `strong` again. The assertion stays on blocking_issues because that is the durable invariant; the band moves with any new warning and would re-couple this case to a number that is not about blocking.

evals.name: impact_reports_both_reference_lists
evals._note: Was `update_needed_in_includes: shared/ontology/artifact-types.json` — two problems. `update_needed_in_includes` is not a key the tool emits (it emits `update_needed_in`), and the assertion encoded a GAP that has since been CLOSED: artifact-types.json now mentions skill-health, so it correctly appears in `referenced_in` and `update_needed_in` is empty. Rewritten to the durable invariant plus the now-true fact. Corrected 2026-08-17.

evals.name: dangling_route_is_blocking
evals._note: A routing.json target that is not an installed skill must appear in blocking_issues.
